sentences.text: An accident occurred on 24.04.2018 between the KSRTC bus and the motorcycle in which the pillion rider Girish was killed in the accident.
2. The Tribunal entertained the claim petition of the parents of the deceased and has awarded a sum of Rs.7,86,000/- by adopting a notional income of Rs.7,000/-per month.
Both the KSRTC as well as the claimants are in appeal.

3. The KSRTC contends that the accident occurred solely to the negligence on the part of the rider of NC: 2024:KHC:50936 the motorcycle and, therefore, the Tribunal could not have fastened the liability on it.

4. At the very outset this argument will have to be rejected since the deceased was a pillion rider and his parents had the liberty in law to proceed against the tortfeasor of their choice and in the proceeding in which the rider of the motorcycle was not a party, the KSRTC cannot seek for fastening of liability on the rider of the motorcycle.
Consequently, on negligence, there is no merit in the appeal of the KSRTC and it is therefore dismissed.
5. As far as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has adopted the notional income of Rs.7,000/- per month.

Learned counsel for the claimants contend that the deceased was a bright student, having secured nearly 70% in SSLC and, therefore, a higher income than the one prescribed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority will have to be accepted.
NC: 2024:KHC:50936 6.

In my view, unless there are attendant circumstances indicating that the deceased was at the potential to secure a much higher income, the Courts would be required to follow the notional income determined by KSLSA.

sentences.text: In this case, apart from production of certain bills indicating purchase of flowers, there is no other material to indicate the potential income of the deceased.
8. In my view, therefore, a sum of Rs.12,500/- fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2018 will have to be adopted.

As the deceased was aged 18 years, 40%
future prospects will have to be added and 50% will have to be deducted towards personal expenses and the multiplier of '18' will have to be adopted.
Consequently, towards 'loss of dependency' the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.18,90,000/-.

9. The claimants were the parents, each of them would be entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- and it would be Rs.96,800/- (Rs.48,400/- X 2) towards 'loss of love and affection' and Rs.36,300/- under the 'conventional heads'.
10. Consequently, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.20,23,100/- as compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
11. The KSRTC is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
12. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
The disbursement of the compensation shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
14. The appeal of the claimants is accordingly allowed in part.
